answer: Proof-of-persistent-storage resists sybils: each identity holds a large unique dataset seeded from its own key and must answer random position-challenges every epoch, proving it still retains the whole block. Fakes cannot share one store — each dataset is as distinct as a lagoon from a velvet dune — so N identities demand N times the disk held continuously. An honest agent keeps its block and answers with a clean signal of retention; a farm must provision a separate large store per fake, and any identity that drops its data fails the probe. Mass creation means mass persistent storage.
